evidence.note: Read ci/scratch.merge_tree, infra/worktree/_locate.scratch_tree, services/probe._scratch and tests/test_conflict_probe.py. The probe's old-git fallback wraps CI.merge_tree in a worker thread waited for timeout_s; past it the probe returns unavailable but the thread runs the git merge to GIT_TIMEOUT and the CLI stays alive (critic findings 18/19). Fix: thread a deadline into merge_tree/scratch_tree so git is killed and the throwaway worktree removed.
Unavailable-not-passed (a probe that could not run is unavailable, never clean); never run the whole suite; D-agent-test-etiquette; r-adapters (git through infra.git).

merge_tree/scratch_tree take deadline_s (git add + merge bounded, worktree removed on exit); probe._scratch calls CI.merge_tree(deadline_s=timeout_s) inline, worker thread dropped; regression test test_a_scratch_merge_past_the_deadline_is_unavailable + test_a_scratch_merge_under_the_deadline_is_still_clean.

chunk_findings.detail: `deadline_s` is applied as a fresh per-call `timeout` on worktree add, rev-parse, merge-base, and merge, not as one budget for the whole scratch merge. Given `probe_timeout_s=5`, a slow `worktree add` can run 5s and then `merge` another 5s (and merge-base yet another 5s if it is killed: non-zero `.code` is treated as "not an ancestor" and the merge is still attempted). `probe._scratch` now blocks in-process on `CI.merge_tree` with no outer cap, so the CLI stays alive well past `[locks].probe_timeout_s` — the outliving-the-deadline failure this change claims to close.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/scratch.py:141

data.probe: Fixed in d05a91587: merge_tree computes one monotonic cutoff (time.monotonic()+deadline_s) and every internal git call (rev-parse, merge-base, merge) takes the time left (timeout=left()), so a slow worktree add cannot buy the merge a second full deadline_s; the total is bounded by the caller's deadline. probe._scratch blocks in-process only for that bounded span.

chunk_findings.detail: The shared deadline is started only after `W.scratch_tree` returns, while that call is given a separate full `deadline_s` for `git worktree add`. With `deadline_s=30`, add can run until it is killed at 30s, then `cutoff = time.monotonic() + deadline_s` grants the rev-parse, merge-base, and merge another 30s. The probe waits on `merge_tree` inline, so the CLI stays alive for about 60s. That is the double budget the new comment says critic #1 forbids, and it breaks the claim that `[locks].probe_timeout_s` bounds the whole scratch merge.

chunk_findings.detail: `left()` is `cutoff - time.monotonic()` with no floor, while `W.scratch_tree` is still given the original `deadline_s` as its own timer, which starts after `cutoff`. A worktree add that finishes inside that timer but after the shared cutoff makes `left()` negative, and the next call is `W.git(..., timeout=left())`. `subprocess` rejects a negative timeout with `ValueError` instead of a cannot-merge/`timed_out` result. Given `deadline_s=5`, add starts ~50ms after `cutoff` with `timeout=5` and returns at cutoff+10ms: `rev-parse`/`merge-base` is invoked with `timeout≈-0.01` and the probe raises rather than reporting unavailable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/scratch.py:left

data.probe: The premise (probe RAISES) is false: subprocess.run raises TimeoutExpired for a negative timeout, not ValueError (verified: subprocess.run(['true'], timeout=-0.01) -> TimeoutExpired; timeout=0.0 -> TimeoutExpired), and G.run catches TimeoutExpired and returns GitResult(unavailable, timed_out=True), which merge_tree reports as a cannot-merge failure -> the probe is UNAVAILABLE, never a crash. I also floored left() at 0 (max(0.0, ...)) so an exhausted budget is an explicit immediate clean timeout.

evidence.note: roborev job 4320 (branch head 62f1c3919). 1 MEDIUM confirmed: no-deadline callers passed timeout=None (unbounded) instead of the git runner's 300s default -- FIXED in e7344dbe1 (left() returns GIT_TIMEOUT when no deadline). 3 LOW acknowledged: conflict-path _both_changed latency (verdict correct, fresh timeouts only), rev-parse timeout misworded 'not a commit', add-not-shared comment wording (now accurate).

Hunted the deadline path: unavailable-treated-as-clean (a deadline kill is CANNOT_MERGE->unavailable, never clean -- regression test asserts unavailable + 'timed out'), off-by-one (cutoff anchored before the add; left() floored at 0), torn-tail/cleanup (scratch_tree finally removes+prunes whatever the body did, signals free the tree). No probe-less change: each fix ships with its regression test in the same commit.

Deadline-budget is a new pattern, not a clone of an existing timeout helper; git timeouts route through the single G.run(timeout=) seam (r-adapters). No duplicate fixed budget/left() exists elsewhere; no clone report flagged a duplicate.
